name: Question 7
problem: Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix $D=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since $D$ is orthogonal, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{-1} & ={D}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Find the inverse of the orthogonal matrix D=[−310−110110−310].

a
[−1010−10−10]
b
[−310−110110−310]
c
[−10−1010−10]
d
[−310110−110−310]
e
D is not invertible
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The inverse of an orthogonal matrix is equal to its transpose.

Therefore, since D is orthogonal, we have

D−1=DT=[−310110−110−310].
